text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ruling Social Democratic Union to discuss at central committee meeting on Saturday the destiny of the coalition with the Socialist Party, its stand towards the new Liberal Democratic Party and results of local elections and its defeat in Skopje.

- Non-government organisations of ethnic Macedonians from Greece, six from the Republic of Macedonia and four from Greece, concluded on Sunday in Skopje that the Greek law that forbids visits to places of origin is against all human rights standards.
- Macedonia expects new laws for reform of the administration. It is possible that future governments will not have deputy prime ministers or ministers without portfolios.

- Very small response (26.2 percent) of voters for one seat in parliament in Gostivar on Sunday. Parliamentary elections in the municipality organized after former ethnic Albanian PDPA MP Rufi Osmani became mayor following local elections in December.
- New Macedonian ambassador to the U.N. Naste Calovski presented his credentials to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan. -- Skopje newsroom, +389 91 201 196
